name: Automatic Task Helper
intro: A desktop tool for turning repetitive browser work into reusable, understandable workflows.
overview: Automatic Task Helper is for browser jobs that are too repetitive to do by hand and too specific to justify a custom integration.
A workflow can combine navigation, clicks, text entry, waits, and conditional steps. The goal is to make useful automation feel more like describing a routine than programming a bot.
challenge: Let people automate fragile browser tasks while keeping every step visible enough to understand, adjust, and trust.
approach: Treat browser work as a sequence of observable actions, then give an agent enough context to help build and recover those sequences without hiding what it is doing.

highlights.title: Reusable queues
highlights.text: Capture a routine once, then run the same sequence again when the work returns.

highlights.title: Human-readable steps
highlights.text: Clicks, entries, waits, and checks stay visible instead of disappearing into code.

highlights.title: Built for the messy web
highlights.text: Conditional steps help workflows handle pages that do not behave exactly the same every time.

next: Improve workflow recovery and make building a first automation faster.
